## Summary
This registrant is a Mexican legal entity whose single MA-L block, 24:7C:46, was assigned on 19 April 2024 to an address on Carretera Base Aérea in Zapopan / Tlajomulco, Jalisco (the Guadalajara metropolitan area) [2][3]. The name and location match Flex Ltd., the Singapore-headquartered electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and ODM company founded in 1969 as Flextronics, which the Wikipedia article ranks as the world's third-largest EMS/ODM by revenue [1] and whose "Guadalajara North" site is at the same Carretera a la Base Aérea 5850 address, alongside Guadalajara South, Juárez, Tijuana, Aguascalientes, Reynosa and San Luis among its Mexico sites [4]; the parent relationship is therefore inferred rather than documented. Flex builds products for other brands - the article cites Mac Pro computers from 2013 and LCD televisions for LG Electronics at Ciudad Juárez [1] - so a MAC in this block is almost certainly a device sold under some other company's name, built at a Flex plant in Jalisco, with the manufacturer's rather than the brand's OUI burned in. Which brands and product types use this 2024 block is not publicly documented in any source reachable in this session (no teardown, FCC filing or device wiki could be found tying 24:7C:46 to a product), so device class, radios, silicon and FCC grantee are all recorded as unknown rather than guessed. For an operator the practical reading is "contract-manufactured, brand unknown": 13 of these on one host suggests a single product line bought in quantity, and DHCP hostname, mDNS or TLS SNI will identify it faster than the OUI will.
